metadata.title: 5 Things to Know Before the Stock Market Opens on Friday

content.text:
Stock futures are pointing lower after yesterday's tech sell-off; cell tower stocks are surging after a report that SpaceX aims to secure thousands of cell sites; American Express raised its profit forecast; Western Digital's earnings are failing to lift the stock; and Deckers Outdoor shares are falling after an earnings miss. Here's what you need to know today.
Stock Futures Point Lower to Wrap Up Volatile Week
Some of yesterday hardest-hit stocks in the AI trade, including Sandisk (SNDK), Micron Technology (MU), and Nvidia-backed (NVDA) Lumentum (LITE), are on the rise this morning. Still, declines in major mobile carriers (more on that below) and software stocks are threatening to hold back a broader rebound. Tech-heavy Nasdaq futures were down 0.1% recently, while futures linked to the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 0.3% and 0.7%, respectively. The Nasdaq and S&P closed sharply lower yesterday amid a sell-off in tech stocks. WTI oil futures were up 1.6% recently at $101.10 per barrel, while gold futures fell slightly to $4,045 an ounce, and bitcoin was little-changed at $81,400. The yield on the 10-year Treasury note, which affects interest rates on loans, was at 5.01% this morning, up from 4.96% yesterday, which marked its first close below 5% in a month.
SpaceX Talks Send Cell Tower Stocks Surging
Shares of Crown Castle (CCI), a leading provider of cell tower infrastructure, were up more than 10% ahead of the opening bell, after a Bloomberg report that the company is discussing leases with SpaceX (SPCX). Shares of American Tower (AMT) also climbed. SpaceX is looking to secure a minimum of 80,000 cell sites across the U.S. as part of its goals to make Starlink Mobile a major mobile carrier, according to the report. Shares of major mobile providers AT&T (T), Verizon (VZ), and T-Mobile (TMUS) were each down about 4% ahead of the opening bell amid worries about competition. SpaceX shares were up 2% recently after plunging 9% yesterday.
American Express Raises Profit Forecast
American Express (AXP) told investors it expects higher profits this year, as affluent consumers keep spending. The credit card provider said it now anticipates full-year earnings per share of $18.30 to $18.60, up from an earlier forecast of $17.30 and $17.90. The company posted adjusted earnings of $4.68 a share for the third quarter, above the $4.49 analysts surveyed by Visible Alpha called for. Its revenue rose 8.9% year-over-year to $20.06 billion, just slightly below estimates. Shares of the Dow component were down 1% in premarket trading.
